mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reduces the discount rate for equity cash flows, leading to higher valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is always active as the current rate level is observed.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1% (over a 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% (over a 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is low (FEDFUNDS < 0.1%) and inflation is high (CPIAUCSL > 235), the market anticipates aggressive rate hikes to combat inflation, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.1% and CPIAUCSL > 235 (over a 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising and CPIAUCSL above 230), reduced liquidity and higher discount rates cause negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising > 0.2pp in 3 months and CPIAUCSL > 230
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods classified as monetary tightening cycles (over a 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: Strong housing starts (HOUST) indicate robust consumer demand and economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days. The signal is always active as the current housing level is observed.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST exceeds 900 (over a 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.0%) signals labor market tightness that may fuel wage inflation, prompting aggressive Fed rate hikes that reduce equity valuations and cause negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE is below 4.0% (over a 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 100) coupled with weak GDP growth (GDPC1 growth < 1.5% annually) indicates economic slowdown, reducing corporate earnings expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100 and GDPC1 growth < 1.5% annually (over a 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (HOUST > 900 and GDP growth > 3% annually), market overvaluation from strong consumer demand leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the cycle matures.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 900 and GDPC1 growth > 3% annually (over a 3-year rolling window).
